content:
According to the Financial Times, the latest court documents show that OpenAI is disappointed with the adoption rate of ChatGPT through Apple Intelligence, stating that its performance is "far below expectations," a situation that emerged after its launch in 2024. Details are as follows.

OpenAI is asking the court to issue a ruling before the trial

In August 2025, Elon Musk stated that X, which has been merged into SpaceXAI, will sue Apple and OpenAI over an alleged conspiracy to exclude competitors in the artificial intelligence industry. The lawsuit stems from the agreement between OpenAI and Apple to integrate ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence and Siri.

After the case was officially filed, the scope of the lawsuit has actually gone beyond the App Store ranking issues that Musk initially publicly complained about. X and SpaceXAI also accused Apple of attempting to suppress the development of "super apps," including X's efforts to establish itself as an "everything app."

In the weeks and months that followed, the companies involved successively submitted statements, allegations, and rebuttals to the court. Apple and OpenAI have repeatedly argued that the agreement is not the exclusive partnership alleged in the lawsuit; court documents filed during the same period have also revealed new details about how the collaboration between the two sides operates.

One of these details was disclosed today in a document filed by OpenAI. According to a report by the Financial Times, OpenAI "expressed disappointment at the low level of interest from iPhone users following the 2024 agreement that brought ChatGPT-powered 'Apple Intelligence' features."

The report is as follows:

Court documents released on Wednesday show that when the agreement was reached in 2024, OpenAI had originally expected to generate a "halo effect" through Apple's promotion and brand partnership, and anticipated gaining more subscriptions from Apple Intelligence users. However, within one month after the ChatGPT integration feature launched, its performance "appeared to have a slow start," and OpenAI immediately downwardly revised its weekly active user growth forecast. The documents indicate that by the summer of 2025, "it had become clear that Apple's integration of ChatGPT had significantly underperformed expectations."

The report points out that several sections of dialogue in today's filing were redacted, but the unredacted portions show that OpenAI executives were concerned that Apple might "want to move faster" to find another AI partner.

When Apple Intelligence was first announced in 2024, Craig Federighi said in an interview that Apple ultimately hoped to allow users to choose between different AI models, specifically mentioning that Google Gemini could potentially become one of the integration options in the future.

That particular partnership ultimately did not materialize, but Apple later turned to using Google's Gemini model to power the new Siri AI; Xcode has also expanded support for coding agent tools from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI.

Returning to today's documents, the Financial Times mentioned that the documents also point out that the way Apple implemented ChatGPT may be one of the reasons for the low adoption rate, because the related integration feature is turned off by default.

Finally, according to Reuters, OpenAI is also arguing that SpaceX's recent securities disclosure documents have undermined SpaceXAI's claim that its partnership with Apple has harmed competition. In its filing, OpenAI stated that SpaceX's IPO registration statement was full of disclosures that were "completely contrary to the competitive harm alleged in the lawsuit."

Based on the above reasons, OpenAI is asking Judge Mark Pittman to issue a ruling in favor of OpenAI on SpaceXAI's antitrust allegations before the trial. The case is currently scheduled to begin in January.

Readers can find the related report in the Financial Times, as well as Reuters' report.
